I start with extra fine ground coffee ( or 'cafe molido' as it is seen on some packaging), cheapest I can get usually is around $2-$4 per pound, but sometimes I get it for a buck fifty. I use 3/4 of a cup of grounds in probably 50 oz of cold water and it steeps for 3 days with a few shakes in between. I generally don't shake it right before I press it and once pressed, it sits for another 12 hours.

I use simple syrup as my sweetener, although I just started making my simple with a bit of molasses and that adds to the body of the coffee the same as using turbinado sugar would. My simple recipe is 2 cups sugar to a cup and a quarter of water, molasses to a dark amber color, boil until sugar crystals dissolve.

For me everything is on a rotation, so I started todays coffee for three days ago. You can get about the same results with a 2 day steep, but there is something that happens between days 2 and 3 where the coffee just seems to press better on the 3 day steep.

The lynchpins of the operation are the glass jars I found lying around here. They have nice seals on them so you can get a good shake on 'em and they're pretty big, probably hold half a gallon.

I've found extravagant ways to complicate what should be a fairly simple process but, all for good reasons. I'm sometimes using cheap and terrible coffee, yet the end product is always generally the same, that was my primary objective.

There is lots of waste. I err to the side of not getting grounds in my coffee so when I dump into the press, I try to keep as much ground out of the press so its not so groundy-tar.
I make some killer cold brew coffee.
